sections.html:
Madison County fills a patch of northeast Nebraska. Madison is the seat of government, while Norfolk is where most of the jobs are. The land is about 575 square miles of gentle, mostly farmed hills, and the Elkhorn River cuts across the upper middle.

Besides those two, Battle Creek, part of Newman Grove, part of Tilden and the village of Meadow Grove are incorporated. Emerick, Enola, Kalamazoo and Warnerville have no municipal government of their own.

Census takers in 2020 found 35,585 people in 14,024 households and 15,094 housing units, of which 7.1% sat empty. Roughly two of every three occupied homes are lived in by their owners (66.0%), and the other 34.0% are rented. The rental vacancy rate was 8.9%. With that many landlords around, a vacant rental is a common reason a house comes up for a fast sale.

A Madison County tax statement for real property is payable by December 31. Half of it turns delinquent the following May 1 and the remainder on September 1. Personal property is on the same calendar.

EventDateResult if missed or met
Tax statement dueDecember 31Full payment can be made from this date
First-half delinquencyThe following May 1Penalty clock starts on the unpaid first half
Second-half delinquencySeptember 1Penalty clock starts on the unpaid second half
Valuation protest filingJune 30Form 422 goes to the county
Appeal of a board ruling30 days after the board adjournsHeard by the state commission

Search and pay on Nebraska Taxes Online for Madison County. For questions, ring the treasurer at 402-454-3311, extension 133, or write to PO Box 270. The courthouse sits at 1313 North Main Street in Madison, Nebraska 68748. Offices shut on November 26 and 27, 2026 for Thanksgiving, so schedule any payoff errand around those days.

Come the due date, tax on personal property attaches as a first lien to everything of that kind you own. Leave it unpaid and the county may seize any of your personal property to cover the debt, whether or not that particular item was taxed.

If you run a business on the land you are selling, request both the real estate balance and the personal property balance before you pick a closing day. Shop tools and equipment on site may count as personal property, which is assessed and billed separately from the land and buildings.

The total on a Madison County bill is a stack of separate levies. For each taxing body the assessor publishes a certification of values. The 2026 set was posted in August 2026 and covers cities, the county, the Ag Society, the Airport Authority, Natural Resources Districts, Educational Service Units, fire districts, Northeast Community College, the Norfolk Parking District, railroad transportation safety, sanitary districts, school bonds and school districts.

Tax increment financing project sheets are posted for Madison, Newman Grove, Norfolk and Tilden. A parcel inside one of those projects may have part of its tax redirected to the redevelopment effort, and the assessor can tell you whether yours is affected.

This office exists to keep values equal across every class of property, using careful mass appraisal and tidy property and land records. Reach it at extension 160, at assessor@madisoncountyne.gov, or by mail at PO Box 250.

Before you list, spend a few minutes on three parts of its website:

  • Online valuation records, which show how your parcel is classified and what it is worth on paper.
  • A definitions page that separates real property, personal property, agricultural land and greenbelt land.
  • Links to the state's homestead exemption rules and to the separate exemption for religious, charitable and educational property.

Online maps layer in parcels, flood plain and zoning. Look at them first if the property is rural or close to the Elkhorn River, the Yellowbanks wildlife management area or Oak Valley.

A valuation protest goes on Nebraska Form 422, and the county Board of Equalization hears it. Real property protests must be in by June 30. State the value you believe is right, say why, and attach support: an appraisal, a contractor's estimate for repairs, or recent sales of comparable houses.

Unhappy with what the board decides? The next stop is the Tax Equalization and Review Commission, and you have 30 days from the board's adjournment to get there.

Begin by asking the treasurer for a payoff on the parcel, covering real and personal accounts. Hand that figure to the title company, which pays it out of your sale proceeds at the closing table. Anything unpaid after May 1 (first half) or September 1 (second half) is delinquent and will show up in the title search.

When you go to the office, bring the parcel number and photo ID. A house held in an estate or trust needs the person signing to carry papers proving authority.

Rental owners should also check that no tenant is behind on the lease before the sale is set, since a vacant or troubled rental can slow a conventional buyer's financing.

The grantor, meaning you as seller, pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax. For deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026 it is $3.32 on each $1,000 of value. Attach Form 521, the Real Estate Transfer Statement, to the deed, because the register of deeds refuses to record a deed that arrives without it.

In a cash sale there is no lender appraisal and no underwriting, so timing depends on title work and on how quickly the tax payoff is settled. For a vacant Norfolk or Madison rental, that can be worth more than squeezing out the last bit of price.

A short order of operations keeps a tax sale from dragging out.

  • Pull up your parcel on Nebraska Taxes Online and note what is paid and what is open.
  • Check the assessor's valuation record and the flood plain map, so you know how the parcel is classified and whether water questions are coming.
  • Ask the treasurer about real and personal accounts if any business equipment stays on the land.
  • Tell the title company about any tax increment financing project covering the parcel.
  • Confirm the deed will go out with Form 521 and that you have budgeted for the stamp tax.

Nothing here requires a lawyer or a trip to the courthouse for most owners, since the records are online and the offices answer by phone. Done in that order, most of what a buyer asks for is already in your hands before the first showing or cash offer.

faqs.q: When are Madison County, Nebraska property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31. Half turns delinquent the next May 1 and the rest on September 1.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the Madison County treasurer's office?
faqs.a: Ring 402-454-3311, extension 133. The assessor answers at extension 160, and both are in the courthouse at 1313 North Main Street in Madison.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Madison County valuation?
faqs.a: Submit Form 422 by June 30 for real property. The Board of Equalization hears it, and a further appeal goes to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days of adjournment.

faqs.q: Do unpaid Madison County taxes create a lien on personal property?
faqs.a: Yes. Tax on personal property is a first lien on everything of that kind you own from the due date, and the county may seize it if the tax stays unpaid.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax when a Madison County house sells?
faqs.a: You do, as the seller. The rate is $3.32 per $1,000 of value on deeds recorded from July 18, 2026 onward, with Form 521 filed alongside.
